facts.reason: Says the Nebraska code leaves out the IRC's 'plumbing, mechanical and electrical chapters (25-33)'. In the 2018 IRC, chapters 25-33 are the plumbing chapters only; mechanical is chapters 12-23, fuel gas is chapter 24 and electrical is chapters 34-43, and Neb. Rev. Stat. 71-6403(1) excludes only section R313 and chapters 25-33. So the IRC's mechanical and fuel gas chapters are part of the state code for one- and two-family dwellings. 71-6406 lets localities adopt plumbing, electrical, fire prevention or 'other standard' codes; it does not name mechanical codes. Checked nebraskalegislature.gov 71-6403 and 71-6406 (Oct. 2026).

fixed.fact: Nebraska's state building code (Neb. Rev. Stat. 71-6403) adopts no International Mechanical Code or International Fuel Gas Code. It adopts the 2018 IRC without section R313 and chapters 25-33, which are the IRC's plumbing chapters (plumbing comes from the 2018 UPC instead), so the IRC's mechanical and fuel gas chapters do apply to one- and two-family dwellings under the state code. For other buildings, mechanical codes and HVAC licensing are left to cities, villages and counties, which under 71-6406 may adopt plumbing, electrical, fire prevention or other standard codes.
